name: Ashok Kumar
bio: I'm an applied AI researcher working at the intersection of natural language processing and finance. I'm currently finishing my PhD in Digital Transformation and Innovation at the Telfer School of Management, uOttawa, which I joined right after completing my Bachelor's at IIT Kharagpur.

My work turns messy, unstructured corporate text (such as earnings calls, filings, and news etc.) into validated, decision-useful signals. To do this I build multi-agent LLM architectures and embedding-based measures and run them at scale: my latest project analyzes 183,000+ earnings-call transcripts (10M+ text segments) on cloud GPU infrastructure to construct a firm-level corporate-integrity index, validated against real financial outcomes. I care deeply about methodological rigor: reproducibility, modeling context, and careful validation and evaluation.

My research has been published in Information Systems Frontiers, the International Journal of Productivity and Performance Management, and PLOS One, with a paper currently under review at ISF journal. Beyond academia, I bring the same toolkit to industry problems including an ML-powered consumer-sentiment system for Honda Canada. I'm honoured to serve as a peer reviewer for Information Systems Frontiers (Springer).
